purpose: Regimen-specific patient treatment information and consent-support content. This module supports, and does not replace, formal consent or local patient-information governance.

green.label: Know
green.meaning: Expected or practical information to understand before and during treatment.

amber.label: Contact
amber.meaning: Symptoms or problems that should be discussed promptly with the oncology team.

red.label: Urgent
red.meaning: Symptoms that may need urgent clinical assessment.

before_treatment: Your oncology team will confirm that the treatment plan, blood tests and other required checks are suitable before treatment.
Bring an up-to-date list of all prescription medicines, over-the-counter medicines and supplements.
Ask which supportive medicines should be taken before treatment, on treatment days and after treatment.
treatment_day: The order and duration of medicines depend on the regimen. Your treatment team will explain what you will receive and how long the visit is expected to take.
Tell staff about new symptoms before treatment begins, even if they seem minor.
between_cycles: Keep the oncology emergency contact details supplied by your treating centre available.
Do not wait for the next clinic visit if you develop a new or worsening symptom that your oncology team has asked you to report.

urgent_general.title: Fever or acute infection symptoms
urgent_general.text: Follow your oncology team's emergency advice if you develop fever, chills, shaking, or feel suddenly unwell.

urgent_general.title: New or worsening breathlessness
urgent_general.text: New breathlessness, chest pain, persistent cough or a sudden change in breathing needs prompt assessment.

urgent_general.title: Severe or persistent diarrhoea / vomiting
urgent_general.text: Contact the oncology team if diarrhoea or vomiting is significant, persistent or associated with dehydration.

urgent_general.title: New neurological symptoms
urgent_general.text: New confusion, severe headache, weakness, seizure, marked drowsiness or other neurological change should be assessed urgently.

urgent_general.title: Unexpected bleeding
urgent_general.text: Report significant bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, or unexplained extensive bruising.

immune_organs.headline: Pneumonitis
immune_organs.symptoms: New cough, breathlessness, chest discomfort or reduced exercise tolerance.

immune_organs.headline: Colitis
immune_organs.symptoms: New diarrhoea, abdominal pain, blood or mucus in the stool.

immune_organs.headline: Hepatitis
immune_organs.symptoms: Yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, marked nausea, abdominal discomfort or abnormal blood tests.

immune_organs.headline: Endocrine inflammation
immune_organs.symptoms: Unusual fatigue, dizziness, headache, thirst, passing urine frequently, temperature intolerance or unexplained weakness.

immune_organs.headline: Immune skin toxicity
immune_organs.symptoms: New or rapidly worsening rash, blistering, painful skin or mouth involvement.

immune_organs.headline: Nephritis
immune_organs.symptoms: Reduced urine, swelling, nausea or kidney-test changes.

immune_organs.headline: Inflammatory toxicity
immune_organs.symptoms: New marked muscle weakness, severe muscle pain or significant inflammatory joint symptoms.

immune_organs.headline: Myocarditis / cardiac inflammation
immune_organs.symptoms: Chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, fainting or unexplained severe weakness.

immune_organs.headline: Neurological immune toxicity
immune_organs.symptoms: New weakness, numbness, vision change, confusion, severe headache, swallowing difficulty or unusual neurological symptoms.

diary_prompt: This prototype diary is intentionally not saved. It is designed to help patients notice and describe changes between treatments without entering identifying information.
footer: Prototype patient-information support. Confirm regimen-specific content against current NCCP/HSE sources, local policy and clinician/pharmacy review before clinical release.
